title: Binary decrement computation
statement: Let $P$ be a register program, let $\mathrm{oracle}$ be a map from decider indices and Boolean words to Boolean answers, let $r$ be a register, and let $dD,dL,dE,dB,\mathrm{next}$ be states. Assume the transitions at these states implement, respectively, the specified binary decrement phases, and assume there are no calls at these states. For every initial configuration $c$ and natural number $n$, there is a time $T$ at which the run started in state $dD$ with register $r$ storing the binary expansion of $n$ and head at zero reaches state $\mathrm{next}$ with that register storing the binary expansion of $n-1$ (with natural-number truncated subtraction) and head at zero; at every earlier time it has one of the states $s$, a tape function $f$, and a head position $q$ such that it is in the corresponding register configuration, there is no call at $s$, and $-1\le q\le |\operatorname{bits}(n)|$.
